image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a chiton (marine mollusk) clinging to a rocky substrate in an intertidal zone. The chiton has a distinct oval shape with a dorsal surface covered in eight overlapping, greenish-brown calcareous plates embedded in a hairy, brownish girdle. Surrounding the chiton are various other marine organisms, including barnacles and small patches of algae or moss on the rock surface.
